title.narrative: Environment, Stakeholders, and Perceptions Analysis for Delivering Humanitarian Response in North-East Nigeria

description.narrative: ltpgtThe ability of humanitarian agencies to address some issues relevant to the humanitarian operation is limited, whether these relate to the operating environment or their ability to reach people in need. The reasons for this may be manifold and may stem from a lack of understanding of who key stakeholders are and how these stakeholders engage in policy-making and/or other decisions with a bearing on humanitarian operations. Similarly, there are gaps in understanding these stakeholders' perceptions of humanitarian actors – and how these perceptions may impact such decisions or the stance/positions that these stakeholders adopt vis-à-vis humanitarian actors. This said, perceptions may, moreover, vary according to the nature and mandate of humanitarian actors, ranging from the Red Cross/Red Crescent movement through international and national/local NGOs to the United Nations system. ltbrgtltbrgtSome of the issues where improved stakeholder engagement is needed, include but are not limited to: protection concerns of civilians access issues bureaucratic impediments and other issues relevant to the operating environment for humanitarian agencies.ltbrgtltbrgtHaving a clear understanding of the most relevant key actors and how they impact the operating environment, including the issues enumerated above, is critical to improving the operating environment and access to people in need. These actors include but are not limited to state and federal level civilian authorities security forces, including the military affected communities – including community and religious leaders media political forums inside and outside of Nigeria and other key stakeholders.ltbrgtltbrgtThe central premise of the stakeholder study is that it will help identify who the key interlocutors are or should be. The study should also map the relationship between these to better understand how policy/decisions are being made. The study will also map out the perceptions these stakeholders hold of humanitarian actors. With this information, an Advocacy Working Group – yet to be formed - within the Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) should be able to identify key influencers and articulate a targeted advocacy strategy that improves stakeholder engagement around critical issues. ltbrgtltbrgtIt is expected that this work will generate: i) an overview of key stakeholders that have a significant impact on the humanitarian operating environment, and protection issues 2) map the impact, interests and perceptions of these stakeholders as it pertains to the humanitarian operations and other factors that may impact on decision making 3) based on the findings of the study, propose measures to improve advocacy in terms of who to engage with and how, i.e. the outline of an engagement strategy. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe scope of the study will focus on the BAY states (Borno, Adamawa and Yobe) but will incorporate the federal level when appropriate, including civil and military authorities, political bodies, opinion makers etc. ltbrgtlt/pgt
